headline: Chinese makers of memory-chip testing equipment are gaining ground in a market where imported machines still make up more than 80% of the installed base in China.
score_reason: Industry trend report relaying other outlets; kept at the pool level.
importance_line: Chinese chip makers rely heavily on foreign test machines, so local suppliers are a step toward self-sufficiency in AI memory, but the market shares come from secondary reports and the Chinese makers are still small.
source: TrendForce News, citing ijiwei and ETNews
summary: TrendForce News, citing the Chinese outlet ijiwei and the Korean outlet ETNews, reports that imported machines still make up more than 80% of the testing equipment installed in China's memory back-end plants, with Advantest holding over 50% of the global market. China's TBSTest is expected to reach nearly 15% of China's market for memory test systems in 2026, as AI-driven demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM) pushes up the need for testing.
notes: Market-share figures are second-hand from ijiwei.
